question: Which military division had become rare in warfare during the Gupta period despite being part of the army in texts?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Chariot**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• During the **Gupta period**, the military structure of the empire included four main divisions as described in ancient texts: **Infantry, Chariots, Cavalry, and Elephants**.
 
• However, by the Gupta period, the use of **chariots** had become **rare**, as they were increasingly considered less effective in warfare compared to other divisions like cavalry and elephants.
 
• The decline of chariots in warfare was due to advancements in technology and changes in military tactics. **Cavalry**, which was faster and more mobile, had largely replaced chariots on the battlefield.
 
• Texts like the **Arthashastra** and other historical sources continue to mention chariots as part of the army, but their use was more symbolic or ceremonial during this period.
 
• The other military divisions, such as **Infantry, Cavalry, and Elephants**, remained prominent and were critical components of the Gupta military system.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Chariot Warfare:**

 
 
• Chariots were a significant part of ancient Indian warfare, especially during the **Vedic period** and earlier periods of history.
 
• They were primarily used in open plains where mobility and speed could be effectively utilized.
 
• By the **Gupta era**, advancements in military tactics and the development of better-equipped cavalry units rendered chariots obsolete for practical warfare.
 
 
 
• **Cavalry:**
 
 
• The **Gupta army** relied heavily on cavalry for its speed and mobility. Horses were easier to maneuver and could traverse various terrains more effectively than chariots.
 
• Cavalry units were equipped with **swords, spears, and bows**, making them versatile in combat.
 
 
 
• **Elephants in Warfare:**
 
 
• Elephants were a crucial component of the Gupta military strategy, used for their strength and ability to instill fear in enemy troops.
 
• They were often armored and carried soldiers equipped with **bows and spears** on their backs.
 
 
 
• **Infantry:**
 
 
• The infantry was the backbone of the Gupta military, consisting of foot soldiers armed with **swords, shields, bows, and arrows**.
 
• They were responsible for holding and defending positions during battles.
 
 
 
• **Symbolic Role of Chariots:**
 
 
• Despite their decline in practical use, chariots retained a symbolic role in **ceremonies and rituals**, representing power and prestige.
 
• They were also depicted in art and literature as a mark of heroic and divine figures.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Gupta Military Advancements:**

 
 
• The Gupta empire is renowned for its military organization, including innovations in **weaponry and strategy**.
 
• Their use of cavalry and elephants demonstrated a shift towards more **dynamic and effective methods of warfare**.
 
 
 
• **Decline of Chariots Globally:**
 
 
• The decline of chariots was not limited to India; it was a global phenomenon. By the time of the Roman Empire and later, chariots were largely replaced by cavalry.
 
• This change was driven by the development of saddles, stirrups, and other technologies that enhanced the effectiveness of mounted soldiers.
